label: late copy-phase steps (recall_idx >= 5), preferring inputs p/k/1/t/j/n/2/u
explanation: Almost entirely a copy-phase unit (98% of mass), concentrated on the last few outputs of long sequences: recall_idx 5-8 (93% of mass), to_go 0-1 (85%), L >= 6. It is silent at the delimiter and nearly silent in the original phase (small blips at t=2). Within those late copy steps it fires on only about 7% of eligible steps. Which ones depends strongly on the input token (p, k, 1, t, j have 4-5x lift; n, 2, u about 2x) and more weakly on prev_tok (3, h, m) and out_tok (c, q, n). Top activations are inputs p/k/1/j at to_go 0 in L=6-8 sequences. Adding token conditions raises precision only to about 0.2-0.46, at a large cost in recall. No simple predicate reaches high precision, so the selectivity among late copy steps is probably distributed over token identities and the hidden state. It does not fire on first occurrences of a token (in_first=1 has 0.1x lift), early copy positions (recall_idx 0-1), or the delimiter.
